subject: Action Required — Evidence for customer VPC segregation and pen-test acceptance criteria
messages:
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@finenterprise.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: security@finenterprise.com
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Evidence request: customer VPC segregation + pen-test acceptance criteria for SIG/SOC2

Hannah / Marcus,

We're preparing the SIG and SOC2 pack for our internal review and need a short, authoritative set of artifacts describing how Redwood treats customer-dedicated VPCs/private deployments. Specifically, we need the items below to close our evidence gaps:  

- A concise isolation matrix that maps: customer VPC network boundaries -> what Redwood-managed control plane components (eg. control-plane API, monitoring, log aggregation) have access, and under what conditions. CSV preferred.
- The pen-test acceptance criteria used for private deployments (what findings are considered out-of-scope vs. require remediation prior to sign-off).
- Executive summary from most recent internal or 3rd-party penetration test relevant to private deployments (redacted where needed).
- Network diagram that highlights permitted egress, NAT/proxy/IP ranges, and default deny controls.

Can you confirm whether you can provide these items by Dec 10? If not, please provide an estimated delivery date and any blockers. We may need a short call with your infra/security engineer to go over the matrix.

Thanks,
Aisha Khan
InfoSec Program Manager
FinEnterprise
security@finenterprise.com

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for the clear list — we can provide that. High level plan:  

1) I will circulate an isolation matrix (CSV) that maps component-level access to customer VPCs. That will include conditional access rules for the private control plane and any cross-VPC management tunnels.
2) Marcus will pull the pen-test acceptance criteria and the redacted summary from the November engagement.
3) Karthik will attach the network diagram and an annotation describing egress controls and IP allowlists.

Target: I can get step 1 & 3 to you by EOD Dec 8; Marcus expects the redacted pen-test summary by Dec 12. If you need anything earlier, tell me what to prioritize and we can escalate.

Would you like a 30-min sync next week to walk through the matrix and acceptance criteria?

Best,

Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@finenterprise.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Evidence request: customer VPC segregation + pen-test acceptance criteria for SIG/SOC2

Aisha, Hannah — attaching the materials we discussed. Summary below.

Attachments included: 
- pen-test-summary-2026-11.pdf (redacted executive summary and full finding categories)
- isolation-matrix.csv (component -> VPC access matrix)
- service-network-diagram.vsdx (annotated)

Short executive notes:  
- The November engagement was a third-party assessment focused on our private deployment surface (customer-dedicated VPC + private control plane). No critical findings against isolation boundaries were reported. Several medium findings were raised related to misconfigured logging permissions in a specific legacy data-collector; that has been remediated and re-tested (see remediation notes column in the CSV).
- Acceptance criteria used for that engagement: Any finding classified as critical or high for cross-tenant isolation, egress controls, or auth bypass must be remediated before customer-facing sign-off. Low/medium with compensating controls are accepted with mitigation tickets and re-test windows. The formal acceptance doc is included in the pen-test PDF (last page).
- Egress: by default private deployments have no unrestricted internet egress from customer workloads; egress is via a managed NAT/proxy with allowlist and per-tenant rules. The VPC-level security groups implement default deny for inbound.

If you need additional artifact hashes or a PGP-signed copy for your evidence repository let me know.

Marcus Lin
Principal Security Engineer, Platform
Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

---
Attachment stubs: pen-test-summary-2026-11.pdf (pdf), isolation-matrix.csv (csv), service-network-diagram.vsdx (vsdx)

Hannah / Marcus,

Received — thank you for the quick turnaround and the detailed notes. The isolation matrix and the annotated network diagram help a lot. A couple of quick follow-ups:  

1) Can you confirm the retention period for flow logs and audit logs for private deployments (we need this for SIG-A5 evidence)? Please include the retention location (Redwood-managed bucket vs customer-managed).
2) For the medium findings you mentioned (legacy data-collector), can you paste the remediation ticket IDs and current status so our audit team can reference them?

We may schedule a brief 20-min call next week to review the CSV with our security engineering lead. If you can provide the log retention detail and ticket IDs in an email today, that will let us close 80% of the checklist.

Thanks again — will follow up with a proposed calendar slot if needed.

Regards,
Aisha Khan
InfoSec Program Manager
FinEnterprise
security@finenterprise.com
On Wed, 15 Dec 2026 at 14:27, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com> wrote:
> Aisha — quick answers inline: 
> 
> - Flow/audit log retention: default retention is 365 days in a Redwood-managed, access-controlled bucket. For customers that require customer-managed retention we support pushing logs to a customer-owned bucket via cross-account replication; that option is documented in the private deployment runbook.
> - Remediation tickets: RDW-3241 (data-collector permission hardening) — status: closed (re-tested 2026-11-24). RDW-3302 (logging config drift) — status: in progress (ETA 2027-01-07).
>
